suppress.notes:
kotlin-reflect 1.6.10 is declared by the Kotlin compiler itself. It sits on kotlinCompilerClasspath beside kotlin-stdlib 2.4.20 and kotlin-script-runtime 2.4.20 - the 2.4.20 compiler pins a four-year-old kotlin-reflect on purpose, and it is not a resolution accident that the stdlib alignment in build.gradle.kts could catch. Overriding a compiler's own pinned dependency to quieten a scanner is the wrong trade. This project's own kotlin-reflect - `compileOnly(kotlin("reflect"))` in vim-engine - resolves to 2.4.20 and is scanned and clean.
CVE-2026-53914 is code execution through unsafe deserialization of *build cache metadata*, which is compiler code. kotlin-reflect does not contain it. It is matched here because NVD publishes one CPE for the whole Kotlin product line - `cpe:2.3:a:jetbrains:kotlin:*` with versionEndExcluding 2.4.20 - and dependency-check maps every org.jetbrains.kotlin artifact onto it, so the match is on the version alone. The same CPE is why the bump was worth making for everything that resolves independently, and why this one artifact cannot be.
Only this CVE is suppressed. CVE-2020-29582 on the same jar is deliberately left visible: it scores 5.3 and so does not fail the build, and the case against it is weaker than it looks - the description says the fix shipped in Kotlin 1.4.21, but the range NVD actually publishes is versionEndExcluding 2.1.0, which does cover 1.6.10. Suppressing a finding on the strength of a disagreement between an advisory's prose and its own data is not a good enough reason.
Delete this when JetBrains moves the compiler's kotlin-reflect pin. The scan will ask.
